# RadioButton

Headers: `winui/ui/input/RadioButton.hpp`, `winui/ui/input/RadioGroup.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/RadioButton.hpp`.

A round option button with a label, one of a set of mutually exclusive choices.

Clicking it (or Space while focused) checks it; clicking an already-checked [RadioButton](#uiradiobutton) does nothing, so the user can turn a lone button on but never off. The button doesn't uncheck the others by itself. Register the buttons with a [`RadioGroup`](#class-radiogroup), which doesn't own them, or use [`RadioButtons`](radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons), which owns and lays out a whole set. [`ui::RadioButton`](#uiradiobutton) is the declarative form of a single button.

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::RadioButtonControl* small = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::RadioButtonControl>("Small", true));
ui::RadioButtonControl* large = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::RadioButtonControl>("Large"));

ui::RadioGroup group;
group.add(small);        // already checked: becomes the initial selection
group.add(large);
group.on_change([](ui::RadioButtonControl* chosen) { /* chosen->text() */ });
large->on_checked_changed([](bool checked) { /* fires for checks and unchecks */ });
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

## `ui::RadioButton`

One radio button. Buttons that choose one value of a property are bound with [ui::selects()](../core/namespace-ui.md#selects): checking one sets the property, the others follow it, and the buttons act as one group for the keyboard (one [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop, arrow keys between them) wherever they sit in the tree. For a plain list of options, [ui::RadioButtons](radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons) is the whole group in one spec; imperative code can still tie loose buttons together with a [RadioGroup](#class-radiogroup).

Example: 
```cpp
enum class Size { Small, Large };
ui::Property<Size> size{Size::Small};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::RadioButton{.text = "Small", .checked = ui::selects(size, Size::Small)},
    ui::RadioButton{.text = "Large", .checked = ui::selects(size, Size::Large)},
}});
```

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::SelectionItemProvider`.

A round option button with a label, one of a set of mutually exclusive choices.

Clicking it (or Space while focused) checks it; clicking an already-checked [RadioButton](#uiradiobutton) does nothing, so the user can turn a lone button on but never off. The button doesn't uncheck the others by itself. Register the buttons with a [`RadioGroup`](#class-radiogroup), which doesn't own them, or use [`RadioButtons`](radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons), which owns and lays out a whole set. [`ui::RadioButton`](#uiradiobutton) is the declarative form of a single button.

Example:

## class RadioGroup

Makes a set of loose [`RadioButton`](#uiradiobutton)s mutually exclusive. Not an element: it holds non-owning observers of buttons owned elsewhere in the tree.

Every registered button that is clicked (or activated with Space or UI Automation) is routed through [`select()`](#select), which checks it and unchecks the rest. The group and its buttons may be destroyed in either order: a button that goes leaves the group, and a group that goes leaves its buttons plain radio buttons. For a headed, laid-out group selected by index, use [`RadioButtons`](radio-buttons.md#uiradiobuttons) instead.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::RadioGroup group;

auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::RadioButtonControl* a = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::RadioButtonControl>("A", true));
ui::RadioButtonControl* b = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::RadioButtonControl>("B"));
group.add(a); // already checked: the initial selection
group.add(b);
group.on_change([](ui::RadioButtonControl* now) { /* now->text() */ });
group.select(b); // programmatic: checks B, unchecks A, fires on_change once
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

### RadioGroup

```cpp
RadioGroup() = default
```

A group with no members.

### ~RadioGroup

```cpp
~RadioGroup()
```

Lets go of every member; the buttons stay as they are.

### RadioGroup

```cpp
RadioGroup(const RadioGroup&) = delete
```

Not copyable or movable: its buttons point at it.

### operator=

```cpp
RadioGroup& operator=(const RadioGroup&) = delete
```

Not copyable or movable: its buttons point at it.

### add

```cpp
RadioButtonControl* add(RadioButtonControl* button)
```

Registers `button` (a non-owning observer) with this group. If the button is already checked and no member has been selected yet, it becomes the initial selection. Otherwise the selection waits for [select()](#select) or a click. A button belongs to one group: adding it takes it out of the one it was in.

### remove

```cpp
bool remove(RadioButtonControl* button)
```

Takes `button` out of the group, keeping its checked state. False when it is not a member. A member that is destroyed leaves by itself.

### select

```cpp
void select(RadioButtonControl* selected)
```

Checks [`selected`](#selected) and unchecks every other member, then fires [on_change()](#on_change) once. Does nothing if [`selected`](#selected) is already the current selection, so clicking the checked button again changes nothing. A click on a member calls it, and an app may call it to select a member from code.

### selected

```cpp
RadioButtonControl* selected() const
```

The current selection (non-owning), or nullptr before anything was selected.

### on_change

```cpp
void on_change(Callback<void(RadioButtonControl*)> handler)
```

Fired once per selection change with the newly selected button, after every member's checked state is updated. Replaces any previous handler.
